text:
Maya Patel: FYI — Enterprise customer (AcmePay) opened an escalation: after yesterday's inference build (model-v2.3-quant) they see large rerank flips for identical inputs. Sending logs and a quick repro.
Carlos Rivera: Oof. Do we have request IDs and timestamps? Any chance input normalization changed (whitespace/tokenization)? :thinking:
Maya Patel: Request IDs: r-1029384756 and r-1029384757. Both use the same candidate set and query, only difference is timestamp. Customer pasted the request body and results. They claim scores changed from 0.82 -> 0.34 for one candidate.
Tom Nguyen: Can you paste a minimal curl we can run? Also what model variant did the request hit (v2.3-int8 or v2.3-fp16)?
Maya Patel: They hit v2.3-int8 (routing shows "model: redwood/rerank/v2.3-int8"). Minimal repro they gave:

```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "how to reset card PIN",
  "candidates": ["reset PIN steps", "card lost", "PIN reset via phone"],
  "top_k": 3,
  "return_scores": true
}
```

Results attached as a small table in the ticket — same payload, different scores across two calls.
Sasha Kim: Two immediate hypotheses: 1) non-deterministic KV cache state leading to hidden context differences; 2) quantization rounding causing small embedding shifts that cascade in dot-product normalization. We saw a micro-change in quant kernels in the last patch.
Carlos Rivera: Also check batching behavior — were these calls served in a batch where padding/truncation patterns changed effective sequence length? That can affect attention masks and final embeddings.
Tom Nguyen: I'll pull the serving logs for the request IDs and check kernel selection and batch id. Also verify seed/determinism flags. If they were routed to different nodes (int8 vs fallback fp16) that would explain it.
Maya Patel: Customer says both calls returned from region us-east-1 and same route. They attached SDK trace showing no retries. Ticket link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ACMEPAY-3421
Eve SupportBot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed: model-v2.3-quant rolled to dedicated canary pool at 2026-03-15T03:21:09Z. No automated rollback triggered.
deploy-bot: @eng-ml flagged: recent quantization changes included asymmetric scaling for embeddings to save headroom.
Carlos Rivera: Can you run a deterministic run against v2.3-fp16 and v2.3-int8 with the exact payload and log raw embeddings (pre-normalize)? Use the debug flag:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"how to reset card PIN","candidates":["reset PIN steps","card lost","PIN reset via phone"],"debug":"embeddings,pre_norm","model":"redwood/rerank/v2.3-fp16","return_scores":true}'
```

Then repeat with model v2.3-int8.
Sasha Kim: If pre-normalize embeddings differ by >1e-3 L2 norm across variants, that's a smoking gun for quantization drift. If they're close, look at normalization/divide by small magnitude values.
Maya Patel: I'll ask customer to run that (they're happy to collaborate) and send us the debug dump. They asked if we can also reproduce on our side against a pinned replica.
Tom Nguyen: I'll repro locally against the canary pool and attach logs. Quick note: there was a packing change in the runtime for token type IDs that could shift token indexes by 1 in edge cases with trailing spaces — worth checking tokenized strings on both runs.
Carlos Rivera: Added: run both with `pad_to_multiple_of` fixed and with explicit `max_length`. Also capture tokenization: `tokenizer.encode(query)` output.
Maya Patel: Customer provided tokenizer outputs for both calls — they match. They also included full candidate list ordering. They stress same input, same SDK version, no concurrency.
Sasha Kim: Next steps for eng-ml: 1) reproduce against dedicated canary; 2) compare raw embeddings; 3) check attention mask / sequence len differences from batching; 4) if quant-induced, propose temporary rollback to fp16 for the affected customer.
Tom Nguyen: I started reproduce run (job id: repro-5521). Initial result: small embedding L2 delta ~0.009 between fp16 and int8 for the top candidate, which after cosine normalization turned into score delta ~0.45 -> 0.36. Pushing full logs to GCS and will paste link.
Maya Patel: Customer said impact is on search relevance for top-3, they want ETA and risk mitigation (customer on Dedicated plan). They're okay with a rollback if we confirm regression.
Carlos Rivera: If repro holds, plan: 1) immediate mitigation: route that customer's dedicated pool to fp16 variant (config change); 2) schedule rollback of int8 quant kernels for rerank-v2.3 while we investigate scaling params. Notify customer of config change and ETA ~30-90m.
Sasha Kim: I'll own the postmortem/metric check: evaluate batch-level score distributions pre/post deploy on 10k random queries and run MSE + Kendall Tau for ranking shift.
Maya Patel: Please keep me posted. I'll relay a short timeline and that we're running a targeted investigation. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Tom Nguyen: Update (10m): repro logs uploaded to gs://redwood-debug/repro-5521/logs.txt. Embedding dump included. Preliminary: quant scales for two heads differ from training-time calibration. Filing infra-ticket to revert kernel patch if needed.
Carlos Rivera: Filing support action: notify AcmePay that we're pausing the canary for their dedicated capacity and routing them to v2.3-fp16. ETA: 45m. I'll draft the customer message.
Maya Patel: Customer reply (via ticket): "Appreciate the quick action. Please confirm once routing change is active — we need to validate downstream metrics." :pray:
Sasha Kim: Noted. After routing change we should run A/A between old and new routing to ensure no other regressions.
Eve SupportBot: action: routing-change requested for AcmePay -> target model redwood/rerank/v2.3-fp16. Request ID: route-7788.
Maya Patel: Thanks. I'll follow up with the customer and close the loop once they confirm their end-to-end checks.
Tom Nguyen: Will post final reproduction artifact and postmortem link here when ready.
Carlos Rivera: Thanks team. We'll keep channel updated.
